unknowns.question: Which GitHub App permission and level reads repository contents read-only, and is any permission (such as Metadata) mandatory or automatic?
unknowns.answer: Request the repository permission Contents: Read-only. GitHub lists commits/{ref}, contents/{path}, git/trees, git/blobs, readme, tarball and zipball under Contents with access 'read' for user access tokens. Also request Metadata: Read-only, which GET /user/installations/{id}/repositories requires and which covers GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}. The levels are Read-only, Read & write and No access. Apps start with no permissions, but a user token still reads public resources. A missing permission returns 403 with an X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions header. Whether Metadata is mandatory or added automatically is not stated on the captured pages, so the design selects it explicitly.

unknowns.question: Does a user access token reach only repositories where the app is installed, which REST endpoints list the reachable installations and repositories, and what installation URL does a user follow?
unknowns.answer: Yes: the token reaches only resources both the user and the app can access, and repository permissions apply to the account where the app is installed. Public repositories stay readable. List them with GET /user/installations (no permission needed) and GET /user/installations/{installation_id}/repositories (needs Metadata read), with per_page up to 100. The install URL is https://github.com/apps/APP-NAME/installations/new, with an optional ?state=. Only a public app can be installed by others. The device-flow request accepts an optional repository_id that narrows the token to one repository. Adding a repository through the API needs a write permission, so the user does it on GitHub.

unknowns.question: Device flow for GitHub Apps: endpoints, parameters, enabling setting, errors, lifetimes, polling interval.
unknowns.answer: Turn on 'Enable Device Flow' (otherwise the token request fails with device_flow_disabled). Call POST https://github.com/login/device/code with client_id and optionally scope=offline_access. It returns device_code (40 characters), user_code (8 characters with a hyphen), verification_uri https://github.com/login/device, expires_in (default 900 s) and interval (default 5 s). Poll POST https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token with client_id, device_code and grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code, with no client secret, no faster than interval. slow_down adds 5 s. Errors come back as HTTP 200 with an error field: authorization_pending, slow_down, expired_token, unsupported_grant_type, incorrect_client_credentials, incorrect_device_code, access_denied, device_flow_disabled, plus bad_verification_code and unverified_user_email. The page names two of these codes twice: expired_token/token_expired, and incorrect_device_code/bad_verification_code. Success returns a ghu_ token with expires_in 28800 and a ghr_ refresh token with refresh_token_expires_in 15897600. The GitHub App page describes the responses as query parameters, so the client should parse both form-encoded and JSON bodies.

unknowns.question: Refreshing a user access token: endpoint, parameters, client_secret for device-flow tokens, rotation, errors.
unknowns.answer: POST https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token with client_id, grant_type=refresh_token and refresh_token. client_secret is 'Required unless the user access token was generated using the device flow', so no secret is needed here. Every refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token. The used refresh token and the old access token stop working, so the vault must replace both atomically and refreshes must run one at a time. bad_refresh_token (invalid or expired) means running the device flow again; a wrong grant type returns unsupported_grant_type. Expiry is on by default but 'an optional feature and subject to change'.

unknowns.question: Ending a sign-in: can a no-secret app revoke, how does the user revoke on GitHub, when does GitHub expire or revoke tokens itself?
unknowns.answer: DELETE /applications/{client_id}/token and /grant need Basic auth with the client secret, so this app cannot use them. POST /credentials/revoke takes no authentication (an authenticated call returns 403), accepts ghu_ and ghr_, allows 60 requests/hour and notifies the token's owner. GitHub describes it for exposed credentials the caller does not own, not for sign-out. The user revokes the app's authorization in GitHub account settings, which revokes its tokens; after that, calls return 401 Bad Credentials. GitHub revokes on its own when a token is pushed to a public repository or gist, after one year unused for OAuth tokens (not stated for GitHub App tokens), when an 11th token is issued for the same user/app/scope, and when enterprise or organization owners revoke SSO. User tokens also expire after 8 hours. Recommended sign-out: delete both tokens from the vault, then point the user to GitHub settings. The exact settings URL page was not collected.

unknowns.question: GitHub token formats and prefixes.
unknowns.answer: ghp_ (classic PAT), github_pat_ (fine-grained PAT), gho_ (OAuth app), ghu_ (GitHub App user access token), ghs_ (installation token), ghr_ (GitHub App refresh token). The token responses confirm ghu_ and ghr_. Lengths of ghu_ and ghr_ are not stated, and installation tokens changed length in 2026, so screen and redact by prefix, not by length.

unknowns.question: Which REST endpoints accept a GitHub App user access token for commits, contents, trees, blobs and archives, and which permission each needs?
unknowns.answer: GitHub's user-access-token list includes GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{ref}, /contents/{path}, /git/trees/{tree_sha}, /git/blobs/{file_sha}, /tarball/{ref} and /zipball/{ref}, plus the two /user/installations endpoints. Each read needs only Contents read. Both endpoints read_github uses today are on the list.

unknowns.question: Registration settings for a desktop device-flow app.
unknowns.answer: Callback URL is optional and ignored for the device flow. Keep 'Expire user authorization tokens' selected (on by default, strongly recommended). Select Enable Device Flow. Deselect webhook Active for an auth-only app. Choose 'Any account' under 'Where can this GitHub App be installed?', because only a public app can be installed by others. Permissions are as in U-1. The name is at most 34 characters and unique; a Homepage URL is required. Leaving 'Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation' off is an inference: it starts the web flow, which needs a callback URL.

findings.problem: The Decision says a 401 means the token was revoked, so the app clears the vault and asks the user to sign in again. No capture supports reading a 401 that way. Following it would throw away a refresh token that is still good for 6 months whenever an access token past its 8-hour expiry is used.
findings.evidence: E-01 line 44 gives only one direction: 'If your app continues to use a revoked access token, it will receive the `401 Bad Credentials` error.' No capture says what status an expired ghu_ token gets, or that a 401 always means revocation. BRIEF.md lines 232-233 say: '401 means revoked (clear and ask to sign in, E-01)'. The refresh plan (BRIEF.md lines 225-229) runs on a timer 'shortly before the 8-hour expiry'. A Windows laptop asleep past that point wakes up holding an expired token, and the agent's next read_github call would wipe the vault.
findings.fix: Reword the claim to what E-01 actually says: a revoked token gets 401, and the status for an expired token is not stated. Change the Decision as follows. Check the access token's expiry before every request and refresh, single-flight, when it is close. On a 401, if the vault holds a refresh token that has not passed refresh_token_expires_in, refresh once and retry the call. Clear the vault only when the refresh returns bad_refresh_token or the retried call still returns 401. Add a test for each path.

findings.problem: The Decision tells a missing permission from a rate limit by a header that the captures do not tie to permission failures, and it leaves the primary rate limit out. A 403 for a primary limit has no retry-after header, so it matches neither rule. A rate-limit 403 that also carries X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions would be reported as a missing permission.
findings.evidence: E-04 line 77 and E-05 line 30 say 'you will receive the `X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions` header in the REST API response'; neither limits it to 403 or permission-failure responses. Prior E-08 line 136: exceeding the primary limit gives '403 or 429' with x-ratelimit-remaining 0, and the client waits until x-ratelimit-reset; no retry-after is mentioned. Line 138: for a secondary limit, retry-after applies only 'if ... present'. BRIEF.md lines 233-234 map '403 with X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions' to a missing permission and '403/429 with retry-after' to GITHUB_RATE_LIMIT. The user's 5,000 requests/hour are shared with every app and PAT acting for them (prior E-08 line 46), so running out of the primary limit is a realistic case.
findings.fix: Check for rate limits first. Map to GITHUB_RATE_LIMIT any 429; any 403 with x-ratelimit-remaining: 0 (wait until x-ratelimit-reset); and any 403 or 429 that carries retry-after or a secondary-limit message. Only after that treat a 403 as a missing permission, and use X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions as a hint, not as the test. Add tests for a primary-limit 403 with no retry-after, and for a rate-limit 403 that also carries the permissions header. Cite prior E-08 lines 136-138.

Only HTTPS github.com root, tree and blob URLs parse. The owner must match [a-z0-9-]+ and the repo [a-z0-9_.-]+. Path and ref segments that are empty, '.', '..', contain backslash, '?' or '#', or contain control characters are rejected. The repository key is lowercased owner/repo.
Repository scope comes only from URLs in saved user messages, capped at 20 repositories. Unsupported URLs grant nothing.

GitHubErrorCodeSchema is the closed set of codes that may cross main->engine: RUN_CANCELLED, GITHUB_INVALID_URL, GITHUB_SCOPE_REQUIRED, GITHUB_PATH_EXCLUDED, GITHUB_REDIRECT, GITHUB_NOT_FOUND, GITHUB_RATE_LIMIT, GITHUB_FORBIDDEN, GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE, GITHUB_TOO_LARGE, GITHUB_UNSUPPORTED_FILE, GITHUB_INVALID_RESPONSE, GITHUB_TIMEOUT.

githubFailure maps each reason to a public ErrorCode and message, always with retry 'never'. NOT_FOUND says the repository 'may be private. This reader supports public repositories without credentials.' RATE_LIMIT is NETWORK_ERROR, 'rate-limited the public reader ... do not paste a token into chat.' FORBIDDEN says 'This reader does not authenticate to private repositories.' Unknown reasons fall back to NETWORK_ERROR.

How a private repository is refused today: GitHubReader.request sends GET https://api.github.com${route} with redirect:'manual', credentials:'omit', cache:'no-store' and the headers Accept, X-GitHub-Api-Version 2022-11-28 and User-Agent 'MoonAliza-public-repository-reader'. It sends no Authorization header, so GitHub answers 404 for a private repository, which becomes GITHUB_NOT_FOUND.

Status mapping: 3xx -> GITHUB_REDIRECT (redirects are never followed). 404 -> GITHUB_NOT_FOUND. 429, or 403 with x-ratelimit-remaining '0' or a retry-after header -> GITHUB_RATE_LIMIT. Any other 401 or 403 -> GITHUB_FORBIDDEN. Other non-OK statuses -> GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE. BRIEF next step 2 (map 403/429 with retry-after to GITHUB_RATE_LIMIT) is therefore already implemented; the retry-after value itself is not surfaced.

Reader bounds: 2 MiB response by declared length and while streaming, 256 KiB file, a 20 s deadline for the whole read, at most 1000 directory entries parsed, 200 entries / 35,000 chars returned, 200 lines / 16,000 chars of text. Only base64 UTF-8 text without control characters is accepted. Symlinks and submodules are refused.
The reader re-checks scope before any request (GITHUB_SCOPE_REQUIRED) and refuses sensitive paths before any request (GITHUB_PATH_EXCLUDED). Sensitive entries are dropped from listings.
Commit pinning: each GitHubReader caches repository:ref -> sha. There is one reader per active run, constructed with the global fetch as its default fetcher.
Error normalisation: stop -> RUN_CANCELLED, deadline -> GITHUB_TIMEOUT, GITHUB_* codes pass through, anything else -> GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE.

Main's readGitHub validates the run context (engine, epoch, capability, running status, project, profile revision, assertConversationPolicy) before and after the read, then returns vault.redact(result). Redaction replaces every non-tombstoned vault secret value.

Engine side: read_github is offered only when the host has readGitHub, the user-supplied repositories are non-empty and the run is not a review run. The engine re-derives scope from saved user messages before asking main. Failures become a tool.failed event plus a JSON {error, message} tool result.
System prompts tell the model that read_github is for 'public GitHub repositories explicitly supplied by the user'.

Engine<->main port: github.read carries only {runId, input} from the engine. The reply is github.result (a string, max 262,144 chars) or github.error with a GitHubErrorCodeSchema code. Main collapses any code outside that enum to GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE.

run.context returns repositories derived from saved user messages. Main's contextSchema caps them at 20 strings of at most 200 chars. General chat (projectId null) may be offered read_github and nothing else.

The public error surface is ErrorCodeSchema, which already contains UNAUTHORIZED and CREDENTIAL_REVOKED; GitHub reads use neither today. Main-thrown codes reach the renderer only if publicMessages maps them; anything else becomes INTERNAL_ERROR.

Vault: values are encrypted with safeStorage, write-once per random UUID ref (saveStaged, then commit, then tombstone, then remove), at most 32,768 bytes. The grant purposes are 'inference' | 'provider-test' | 'research' | 'provision'. provider-test and research grants are capped at 30 s. withSecret checks the grant before and after reading the file.

Startup reconcile deletes tombstoned refs and staged refs that are not in the reference set. The set is engine vault.references plus collectorSettings.references(); a new main-owned GitHub account file would have to add its refs here.

Inference grants use contextId = runId (125 s) and are revoked after every model step. Run end, cancel, session-policy change, trust revoke and profile credential change also call revokeContext(runId).

Pasted collector token: research.collector.save accepts a printable-ASCII token (1..16384). CollectorSettings stores only a vault ref in <userData>/research-kit/collector.json and uses the retiredSecretRef crash-safe rotation pattern. The renderer sees only tokenConfigured.

The collector token is decrypted only inside a 30 s 'research' grant, into the child environment as RESEARCH_KIT_GITHUB_TOKEN, with nothing inherited (no GITHUB_TOKEN). Watches can run up to 3,600,000 ms.
The collector needs Actions read and write and dispatches workflows. A read-only-contents GitHub App token cannot replace it.

facts.claim: The vault is main-process only. It is constructed at startup over <userData>/vault with Electron safeStorage as its cryptor and the initial epoch 'starting'. Its doc comment says consumers get a capability, never a credential retrieval API.

A secret is one opaque UTF-8 string of at most 32,768 bytes. It is refused with ENCRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE when OS encryption is unavailable, and written encrypted to <uuid-v4>.bin (mode 0600, fsync) as a 'staged' entry. The ref must match a UUID v4 pattern.

A vault index entry holds only state ('staged'|'committed'|'tombstoned') and createdAt. There is no kind, owner, label or expiry field, so the vault itself cannot record an 8 h or 6-month lifetime or tell which component owns a ref.
No secret can be updated in place. Rotation means saveStaged(new) -> commit(new) -> tombstone(old) -> remove(old), each with a new ref. profile.save and the collector's retire both do exactly this.

The startup reconcile commits staged refs that are in the given set, and deletes staged refs not in the set as well as tombstoned entries. It never removes a committed entry, even one nothing references. The set is the engine's 'vault.references' (DISTINCT profile_revisions.secret_ref) plus collectorSettings.references().

CredentialBinding.purpose is exactly 'inference' | 'provider-test' | 'research' | 'provision'. A grant binds epoch, purpose, contextId, secretRef, optional profileRevisionId and expiresAt. There is no GitHub purpose. shared/host.ts duplicates the purpose list in PurposeSchema, and that schema is used only by tests.

The vault caps grant lifetime only for 'provider-test' and 'research' (at most 30 s). 'inference' and 'provision' have no vault cap. infer() takes a 125 s grant, profile.test 30 s, and collector launch and import 30 s.

Grants live only in memory. setEpoch clears them all and runs on every engine (re)start through the restarted hook. revokeContext clears one context and runs on run end, cancel, project trust revoke and session policy update. tombstone revokes every grant on a ref synchronously, before the disk write.

withSecret checks the grant against the binding before and after reading the ciphertext, then passes the decrypted string to a callback. infer() calls revokeContext(runId) in finally, which revokes every grant whose contextId is that runId.

Redaction matches exact values only. redact() decrypts every non-tombstoned entry (staged included) and replaces each whole value with '[redacted]', longest first. If any entry fails to decrypt it throws REDACTION_UNAVAILABLE. No prefix or pattern token scanner exists anywhere in src: a grep for GitHub token prefixes finds nothing.

Consumers of redact: screenCompletion runs on every completion and checks the tool-call JSON and its leaves, plus provider-state leaves and content. Any change there is PROVIDER_PROTOCOL_ERROR, and then the content is redacted. Also redacted: GitHub read results, command output, review supervisor output and the research document reader.

Today's GitHub reader is one GitHubReader per active run, constructed with no fetcher, so it uses Node's global fetch, not an Electron session. It sends GET only, to constructed https://api.github.com URLs, with redirect 'manual' (any 3xx becomes GITHUB_REDIRECT), credentials 'omit', cache 'no-store', no Authorization header, a 20 s deadline and a 2 MiB bound, and pins the commit per run.

GitHub read failures: 404 gives GITHUB_NOT_FOUND. 429, or 403 with x-ratelimit-remaining 0 or retry-after, gives GITHUB_RATE_LIMIT (the brief's step 2 mapping already exists). Any other 401 or 403 gives GITHUB_FORBIDDEN. A code reaches the engine only if it is in GitHubErrorCodeSchema, otherwise it becomes GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE. The public messages say the reader is public-only and unauthenticated.

Repository scope comes only from github.com URLs in the session's saved user messages (at most 20). The engine checks it, and main checks it again through run.context. read_github is offered only when such repositories exist and the run is not a review run.

Main's readGitHub re-validates the run (epoch, capability, status, profile revision, conversation policy) before and after the read and returns vault.redact(result). The engine then stores the output in a tool.completed event.

The tool description, the system prompts and the spec all say private authentication is not supported. ARCHITECTURE and HANDOFF say GitHub credential storage and private-repository connection are not implemented.

The precedent for a main-owned credential setting is CollectorSettings. It keeps a strict file {version, revision, repository, workflow, ref, secretRef, retiredSecretRef, lastRequest, updatedAt}. Saves are compare-and-set and replay by request id, with an inputHash that covers only whether a token was supplied, never its value. A missing or invalid file reads as 'not configured'. references() feeds the reconcile, and the renderer sees only tokenConfigured.

How the existing GitHub token is used: the research collector token takes a 30 s 'research' grant per use with a unique contextId (import:<job>:<uuid> / collector:<job>:<uuid>). It goes only into a Bearer Authorization header, or the child's env block. Redirects are not followed and the grant is revoked in finally.

Model-profile credentials: StoredProfileSchema is ProfileSchema minus hasCredential plus an optional secretRef, persisted in engine SQLite (profile_revisions.secret_ref). The public Profile exposes only hasCredential. ProfileKindSchema is openai-compatible | openai-responses | anthropic | ollama. A GitHub account is not expressible as a profile without pushing its ref into engine history.

profile.save runs in main. It validates the endpoint, does a revision CAS, and refuses to carry a credential to a new endpoint or kind (CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE). It then stages, has the engine save, commits, aborts runs on the old profile, and tombstones and removes the old ref. profile.delete is declared main-owned, but main has no case for it, so it returns NOT_IMPLEMENTED.
The engine-owned SettingsSchema has no credential fields.

The IPC registry is MethodSpec in src/shared/params.ts, not contracts.ts. Each method has strict params and result zod schemas, an owner (main|engine), an effect and an authorization rule. contracts.ts holds the DTOs, such as Profile with hasCredential, plus DateTimeSchema and HttpUrlSchema.

The bridge accepts calls only from the expected main frame and refuses inputs over 2,000,000 chars. It parses each result with the method's strict schema, and a result with extra fields fails. Errors cross only as mapped codes with fixed messages, else INTERNAL_ERROR.

ErrorCodeSchema already has CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE, CREDENTIAL_REVOKED and UNAUTHORIZED, but publicMessages has no text for CREDENTIAL_REVOKED or UNAUTHORIZED. The vault's CREDENTIAL_CAPABILITY_DENIED and REDACTION_UNAVAILABLE are not public codes, so they surface as INTERNAL_ERROR. ENCRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE has a message.

external.open is main-owned and user-confirmed. It accepts any HttpUrlSchema URL (http/https, no userinfo or fragment) and calls shell.openExternal.

risks: Redaction gap: storing both tokens as one secret string means neither is redacted, because redact replaces only the whole decrypted value (src/main/vault.ts:192).

Refresh-token rotation plus a crash: if GitHub replaces the refresh token on every refresh (open in the design contract, U-4), a crash between receiving the new pair and committing refs and the file loses the only valid refresh token and forces a re-sign-in. The order must be stage, then file, then commit, then retire, as in src/main/collector-settings.ts:64-81.

Concurrent refresh: two runs refreshing with the same refresh token can make the second fail with bad_refresh_token and wrongly sign the user out. Refresh must be single-flight, e.g. serialized() in src/models/artifact-files.ts:59.

Epoch coupling: grants are bound to the engine epoch and wiped on any engine restart (src/main/vault.ts:55-58; src/main/index.ts:178). An account-level refresh or sign-in grant that spans a restart fails with CREDENTIAL_CAPABILITY_DENIED and must be retried, not treated as revocation.

contextId collision: infer() calls revokeContext(runId) in finally (src/main/index.ts:104). A GitHub grant keyed on the bare runId can be revoked by an overlapping inference. Use distinct contextIds (as the collector does) and revoke them explicitly on run end.

Orphaned committed tokens: the reconcile never deletes committed entries (src/main/vault.ts:106-121), and an invalid settings file reads as 'not configured' (src/main/collector-settings.ts:30-33). A retired access token stops being redacted once removed (src/main/vault.ts:172-181, 186), yet it may stay valid at GitHub for up to 8 h.

How a GitHub read handles a response: 3xx is GITHUB_REDIRECT; 404 is NOT_FOUND; 429, or 403 with x-ratelimit-remaining 0 or a retry-after header, is GITHUB_RATE_LIMIT; 401/403 is FORBIDDEN. The body is read as a stream and capped at 2 MiB, then parsed as strict UTF-8 JSON. Its text is never echoed.
The per-call deadline pattern is AbortSignal.any([stop, AbortSignal.timeout(20_000)]). A Stop maps to RUN_CANCELLED, the timeout to GITHUB_TIMEOUT, and any other failure to GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE.

The verified import's authenticated GitHub request uses Node's global fetch by default. The token is decrypted only inside vault.withSecret through a 30-second grant and sent only in that request's Authorization header. The vault is main-only. Each secret is encrypted with safeStorage in its own <uuid>.bin file (mode 0o600) and indexed in index.json. Values over 32,768 bytes are refused, and so is any save when OS encryption is unavailable (ENCRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE).

Vault grants have a fixed purpose: 'inference', 'provider-test', 'research' or 'provision'. Each grant is bound to epoch, contextId, secretRef and profileRevisionId. Only 'provider-test' and 'research' grants are capped at 30 s. withSecret re-checks authorization before and after reading the file.

Startup reconcile commits staged entries that are referenced and deletes unreferenced staged and tombstoned entries; committed entries are kept. Main feeds it the engine's references plus collectorSettings.references(), so any credential reference kept outside the engine database has to be added here.
vault.redact decrypts every non-tombstoned entry and replaces each WHOLE decrypted value with [redacted]. It is applied to command output, model completions and GitHub read results.

CollectorSettings is the precedent for a credential reference that main owns outside the engine database. It is a bounded JSON file holding secretRef and retiredSecretRef. Saves are compare-and-set by revision and replay by clientRequestId with a hash that excludes the token. The sequence is: saveStaged, then atomicJson, then commit; retiring a token tombstones it and then removes it. A missing or invalid file reads as 'not configured'. Its public view carries only tokenConfigured.
File helpers: atomicJson writes a temp file, fsyncs it and renames it into place; boundedJson reads with a size cap; serialized() is a per-path promise lock.
The renderer's collector-token input is an uncontrolled ref, never React state or a DOM attribute, and it is cleared after a save.

15-min flow needs: a status the renderer can re-read after a reload or remount, because pushes are lost when nobody is listening. A remount must never request a new device code automatically (the brief cites 50 code submissions per hour per app).
15-min flow needs: an injected now() and sleep() in tests and short fake intervals. Vitest allows 15 s per test, Playwright 60-120 s, and the Windows job 35 minutes.
invariants: Tokens (access and refresh) and the device_code never reach the engine, the SQLite database, events, logs, the renderer, argv, command environments or any file in clear. They exist only in main's memory during a request and encrypted in the vault (AGENTS.md:80; engine.ts:39-41; index.ts:70 passes process.env to commands, so tokens must never be placed in process.env).

The renderer gets only status, user_code, a fixed verification URL, expiry and signed-in state, never a secretRef. This is the same as tokenConfigured (collector-settings.ts:88-90) and the profile schema, which rejects secretRef (tests/contracts.test.ts:65-82).

A credential is sent only in an explicit Authorization header (or form body) to a fixed GitHub host. Redirects are never followed with it (github.ts:15, 19; research-import.ts:35-44), and no session cookie or HTTP authentication rides along (credentials 'omit', inference.ts:179-183).
Each token is stored as its own vault entry, so that vault.redact, which replaces each whole decrypted value, redacts each token wherever it appears (vault.ts:183-195).

Vault writes follow staged, then settings file, then commit; a replaced token is tombstoned before it is removed. Every reference kept outside the engine database is fed to the startup reconcile (vault.ts:81-121; index.ts:181-184; collector-settings.ts:51-91).
Grants are bound to the engine epoch and are cleared on any engine restart (vault.ts:55-58, 129-154). A refresh re-grants and never caches a decrypted token.
No refusal or error carries GitHub's response text, and only mapped codes cross the bridge (bridge.ts:53-57; github.ts:19-25; tests/github-read.test.ts:38-41).
The renderer stays network-less. External pages open only in the system browser through shell.openExternal, never in the app window (index.ts:306-315; index.html:2).
The public read_github path stays unauthenticated until the private-repository step deliberately changes it (github.ts:15-16; tests/github-read.test.ts:13-14; e2e/github-reading.spec.ts:36).
Quit is never blocked indefinitely: before-quit aborts first and awaits bounded closes (index.ts:324-336; collector.ts:162-171).
A missing or corrupt sign-in settings file must not abort app start (index.ts:320) and reads as signed out (collector-settings.ts:31-33).

Owed by the new work (not present yet): device-flow unit tests on a fake GitHub listening on port 0 for authorization_pending, slow_down (+5 s), expired_token, access_denied, device_flow_disabled, a cancel mid-wait, a quit mid-wait, and an engine restart mid-flow; a test that device_code and the tokens never appear in any push, result or file; a refresh single-flight test; a Windows e2e of sign-in and sign-out with a userData byte scan.
risks: Transport choice. Existing GitHub calls use Node's global fetch (github.ts:12; research-import.ts:69), but decision 4 asks for Electron networking with the system proxy and normal certificate validation (decisions.md:8). How Node fetch handles the Windows system proxy and certificate store is unverified, and the packaged app ignores NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS (ARCHITECTURE.md:49). Sign-in could work on one transport and fail behind a corporate proxy or TLS inspection on the other.

Testability follows from that choice. If sign-in uses session.fetch, the e2e technique of stubbing globalThis.fetch through app.evaluate (github-reading.spec.ts:31-46) does not intercept it, and github.com is a fixed host, not a user setting. Either inject a fetcher seam that the e2e can replace in main, or add a github.com TLS fake, which turns the SAN pin at tests/github-tls.test.ts:36 red.

The providers session uses the system proxy, and credentials 'omit' does not withhold a cached Proxy-Authorization (ARCHITECTURE.md:35). This is acceptable for GitHub, but it must be stated in the spec.

external.open accepts any http(s) URL with a query and calls shell.openExternal without further checks (params.ts:154; index.ts:300). Its 'user-confirmed' authorization is not enforced (contracts.test.ts:59 only checks that it is truthy). A verification_uri relayed from the network or the renderer could open an arbitrary page, so open a constant URL or validate it exactly in main.

Storing both tokens in one JSON vault entry would defeat redaction of each token (vault.ts:187-193). Every redact call also decrypts every entry, so refreshes every 8 hours pile up entries unless the old references are tombstoned and removed.

Concurrent refreshes, from two runs or from a refresh racing a re-sign-in, can each spend the refresh token and get bad_refresh_token. Serialize them (serialized() in artifact-files.ts:59-63) and make the refresh single-flight.

An engine restart clears every grant (vault.ts:55-58; index.ts:178), so a refresh in flight can fail with CREDENTIAL_CAPABILITY_DENIED. Re-grant per attempt, and keep the device flow itself independent of the engine and the epoch.
A new vault purpose has no lifetime cap unless one is added at vault.ts:135. Reusing 'research' would mix GitHub sign-in grants into research revocation semantics.

Quit and crash windows: a token received during before-quit, or between saveStaged and the settings write, is deleted by the next reconcile, which is fine. One received after the settings write survives only if its reference is fed to the reconcile at index.ts:183. The flow must not add an unbounded await to before-quit.

A 15-minute operation implemented as one IPC call would hold a pending invoke and lose its result on a renderer reload. Pushes are dropped when the window is gone (index.ts:158). The renderer needs a status-read method, and a remount must not request a fresh device code (the brief cites a limit of 50 code submissions per hour per app).
Waits based on setTimeout drift across system sleep or hibernation. Check expiry against the clock after each wake, and treat GitHub's expired_token as authoritative.

New error codes that are not added to ErrorCodeSchema and publicMessages surface as INTERNAL_ERROR (bridge.ts:54), and the renderer sees only messages (preload/index.ts:9). Model sign-in states as data, not errors.

Source-text pins on src/main/index.ts (provider-screen, anthropic-transport, ollama-locality) break if code is placed between infer() and readGitHub(), or between the profile.test case and the next case. Keep the logic in its own module.
Vitest's node project runs with isolate:false (vitest.config.ts:12), so a test that stubs global fetch leaks into other files. Inject the fetcher.
The e2e and native checks cannot run in this Linux container (AGENTS.md:41-43). Proof needs a green Windows CI run on the exact head, within the 35-minute job budget (windows.yml:11).

The collector token (a user-entered token for workflow dispatch, collector-settings.ts) and the sign-in user token are different credentials with different permissions. Do not reuse one for the other or share their settings files and references.

Changing read_github to send a token (a later step) changes a recorded contract: it breaks github-read.test.ts:14 and github-reading.spec.ts:36 and contradicts ARCHITECTURE.md:38, github-url-reading.md:9 and the tool description at shared/github.ts:9. Do that deliberately in its own commit, not as a side effect of the sign-in.

gaps.what: Register and own the GitHub App. Someone has to decide which account owns it (the user's personal account or an organization), what it is called (at most 34 characters and unique on GitHub; 'MoonAliza' may already be taken), what Homepage URL it uses, and that it is set to 'Any account'. They then pass back the client ID and the app slug.
gaps.why: The device-flow client needs the client ID as a build-time constant, because the repository has already rejected a production switch for this kind of routing (docs/specification/research-journeys.md:11). The install link the Decision shows, https://github.com/apps/APP-NAME/installations/new (E-12), needs the slug. Only the account owner can create the registration. The owning account also carries GitHub's per-application limits for every MoonAliza install.
gaps.close: Ask the user once. Write the design with named placeholders for the client ID and the slug until the values arrive. Both are public identifiers, not credentials: no client secret is generated or shipped.

gaps.what: Choose the permission scope now, because the approved plan says something different. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-02-research-jobs.md:426 says sign-in 'would replace pasted tokens for private repositories and the research collector'. Line 491 approves 'one secure GitHub connection ... shared by research collection, private repository reading and the steps below' (CI evidence, Actions runs, Issues and PR writes). The research and the maps instead design Contents and Metadata read-only, and keep the collector on its pasted Actions-write token. Separately, the map adds 'Claude and OpenAI use API keys' text to the Model profiles dialog, which is outside this run's 'GitHub sign-in only' scope.
gaps.why: Permissions are expensive to widen after release. Each installing account owner is prompted to approve new permissions, and until they do, their installation keeps the old ones (choosing-permissions capture line 57, E-04). If the collector shared the connection, every refresh would kill the old access token (E-02) while a collector child might still hold it, since a watch can run up to 3,600,000 ms (src/adapters/research-kit/collector.ts:50). The facts for the broader choice are already in the corpus: dispatches, runs and artifacts are all on the user-token list (E-06 lines 141, 193, 225). What is missing is the user's choice.
gaps.close: Ask the user one question. Option (a): read-only private reading now, the collector keeps its token, and a correction note goes into the plan. Option (b): register with the broader permission set now. Drop the Model-profiles text from this build unless the user asks for it.

gaps.what: Decide how private code is treated. In a cloud-allowed session, private repository text that read_github reads is sent to the cloud provider. It is also stored, full-text indexed (src/engine/migrations.ts:94-103) and sent to the renderer through tool.completed. General chat has no project trust gate, and read_github may be offered there (src/main/index.ts:67,93). The spec's consent sentence covers only 'the scoped public lookup' (docs/specification/github-url-reading.md:11). Three sub-choices are also open: whether to send the token on public reads, which moves them to the user's shared 5,000/h bucket and ties the user's identity to every public read; whether a token failure on a public repository falls back to an unauthenticated read; and whether signing out purges private text already read.
gaps.why: These choices decide the consent UI, whether readGitHub needs an extra policy check, the composer text (src/renderer/App.tsx:237) and the spec rewrite. They are product and privacy decisions, not facts.
gaps.close: Ask the user one question; it can be combined with the scope question. Proposed default: the same rules as local project files. Private reads are allowed after the user pastes the URL; local-only stays local; history is kept; the token is sent only when signed in.

gaps.what: The build branch is missing the evidence the new brief rests on. The brief's 'Prior E-xx' citations live in docs/research/2026-10-12-app-sign-in. They cover the rate limits behind the D-3 and D-7 dismissals, the response-encoding resolution, F-3's fix (prior E-08 lines 136-138) and the 50 submissions per hour. That project is committed only on branch research/app-sign-in (5389cd1). It is not on main@0815f42 or on research/github-sign-in. The new project itself is still untracked (git status: ?? docs/research/2026-10-13-github-sign-in-design/).
gaps.why: A builder on the build branch cannot check the claims the design rests on, and handoff cannot pass for a corpus that was never committed.
gaps.close: Merge research/app-sign-in (docs only) into the build branch. Commit the new nested project including research/raw/.fetches.jsonl (its own .gitignore line 32 already un-ignores it). Run handoff.mjs with each project directory as the working directory.

gaps.what: VERIFY F-2 is still open: the not-installed case, who may install on organizations, and SAML. No capture says what status GitHub returns for a private repository the app is not installed on. None says who may install on an organization or another user's account (owner, member request, approval), or what a SAML-protected organization returns (E-01 line 34). Owner pages to collect: docs.github.com/en/apps/using-github-apps/installing-a-github-app-from-a-third-party, docs.github.com/en/apps/using-github-apps/requesting-a-github-app-from-your-organization-owner, docs.github.com/en/apps/sharing-github-apps/making-a-github-app-public-or-private, and docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/troubleshooting-the-rest-api.

The Decision's 'a 404 shows the install link' leads nowhere for organization members who are not owners and for collaborators. gaps.what: The research and the map disagree on what a 401 means (VERIFY F-1). The Decision says '401 means revoked (clear and ask to sign in, E-01)'. The map's touchpoint for src/main/github.ts:19-23 says refresh once, retry once, then report sign-in-required. No capture says what status an expired ghu_ token gets; E-01 line 44 covers only revoked tokens. The Decision's refresh runs on a timer 'shortly before the 8-hour expiry'.
gaps.why: A Windows laptop that wakes from sleep after the expiry still holds an expired token. Under the Decision's rule, the next read would wipe a refresh token that is still good for up to 6 months.
gaps.close: No collection needed. Adopt F-1: check expiry before each request and refresh single-flight when close. On a 401, refresh once if the refresh token is still within refresh_token_expires_in, then retry. Clear the vault only on bad_refresh_token, or when a call with a fresh token still gets 401. Add a day-one test: send a token past its expiry and record the status.

gaps.what: How a 403 is classified (VERIFY F-3). The Decision maps '403 with X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions' to a missing permission. The captures say that header comes back on REST responses in general, not only on permission failures (E-04 line 77, E-05 line 30). The code already checks rate limits first (src/main/github.ts:21). But a secondary-limit 403 with neither retry-after nor x-ratelimit-remaining 0 ('Otherwise, wait for at least one minute', prior E-08 line 138) falls through to GITHUB_FORBIDDEN. Once signed in, that message would claim a permission or installation problem. The exact wording of the secondary-limit error message was not captured.
gaps.why: It breaks the invariant 'errors never claim a cause that was not observed', and the spec rule that response bodies are never surfaced limits how the case can be told apart.
gaps.close: Design decision, no collection. Map a 403 without rate-limit headers to an ambiguous FORBIDDEN that lists the possibilities: no access, app not installed, SAML, or a secondary limit. Use X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions only as a hint. Optionally match the body internally without echoing it. Add tests for a primary-limit 403 without retry-after and a rate-limit 403 that also carries the permissions header.

gaps.what: The brief's 'prefix secret screen' does not exist in the repository. The Decision says 'add ghu_, ghr_, gho_, ghp_, ghs_ and github_pat_ prefixes to the secret screen'. MoonAliza has no prefix screen. Its screen is exact-value vault redaction (src/main/vault.ts:183-195), used by provider-screen.ts:33-46 and readGitHub (src/main/index.ts:122).
gaps.why: A new prefix screen would change read_github output for private repositories that contain such strings, such as fixtures or docs, and nothing defines whether a match is redacted or refused. It would also trip provider-screen's 'redact changed the text, so PROVIDER_PROTOCOL_ERROR' rule (provider-screen.ts:37-43) whenever a model tool call quotes such text.
gaps.close: Design decision. Store each token as its own vault entry so exact-value redaction catches it (as the map's invariant says). Use the prefixes only to validate the shape of the token response. Drop the screen bullet or define it narrowly.

gaps.what: The research and the map disagree about a repository listing. The Decision and next step 3 add a 'repositories I can read' view built on GET /user/installations and /user/installations/{id}/repositories (E-07). The map's invariant says sign-in grants no listing of the user's repositories, and that scope stays limited to URLs in saved user messages (src/shared/github.ts:24-31).
gaps.why: This decides the new MethodSpec methods (and the exact key list pinned in tests/contracts.test.ts:42-60), whether listing results could ever reach the model, and part of the reason for requesting Metadata.
gaps.close: Design decision: a listing shown only in the UI (main to renderer), never offered to the engine and never widening scope, or no listing in v1.

gaps.what: The refresh lifecycle is not mapped against Stop, the 20 s deadline, quit, engine restart and sign-out. A read runs under AbortSignal.any([stop, 20 s timeout]) (src/main/github.ts:38). before-quit aborts every run (src/main/index.ts:327). An engine restart calls vault.setEpoch, which clears all grants (src/main/index.ts:178; src/main/vault.ts:53-56). The map covers single-flight refresh but not whether a refresh can be cancelled, nor what happens to a read in flight when the user signs out.
gaps.why: Once GitHub issues the new pair, the old one is dead (E-02). A refresh aborted after its request is sent therefore loses both tokens and forces a new sign-in. That puts the 'Stop discards late results' invariant at odds with staying signed in.
gaps.close: Design rule, no collection. The refresh runs on a main-owned signal, outside the run's stop and the 20 s deadline. Quit waits, with a bound, for an in-flight refresh to persist. Decide whether the GitHub grant is tied to the engine epoch. Sign-out tombstones the refs (vault.tombstone revokes grants synchronously), and reads in flight fail with CREDENTIAL_REVOKED. Add tests for each.

gaps.what: How the renderer learns the device-flow status is not mapped. Pending, slow_down, expired, denied and success all have to reach the renderer. The map lists request methods only. The existing push channels are 'moonaliza:event' and 'moonaliza:research' (src/main/index.ts:158,160; src/preload/index.ts:12-20).
gaps.why: This decides whether to add a new preload channel with its own schema and contract tests, or to have the renderer poll github.account.read. Either way, device_code must never cross.
gaps.close: Read src/preload/index.ts and src/shared/contracts.ts, then choose between polling and a typed 'moonaliza:github' status channel.

gaps.what: VERIFY F-4: whether the refresh-chain exemption holds. E-02 line 79 exempts client_secret per token: 'Required unless the user access token was generated using the device flow'. No capture says whether a token produced by refreshing a device-flow token still counts as generated by the device flow.
gaps.why: If it does not count, every user has to sign in again every 8 hours, and the 6-month design fails.

gaps.what: The device-flow cap per application and the GitHub App rate limits are unverified. '50 submissions in an hour per application' comes from the OAuth-apps page (prior E-01 line 307). Owner page: docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/rate-limits-for-github-apps.

gaps.what: Choose the network stack for the GitHub calls. The reader, and the new device-flow client, use Node's global fetch (src/main/github.ts:12), which does not use the Windows system proxy. Model providers use an Electron session (src/main/index.ts:66,98). Keeping global fetch is required by the e2e patch (e2e/github-reading.spec.ts:31-45).
